name: Two-dimensional lane-free models: Mixed Traffic Model (MTM, Kanagaraj and Treiber 2018), Intelligent-Agent Model (IAM, Treiber and Chaudhari 2023), Non-Lane-Based IDM (NLBIDM, Chennai)
type: model (family of microscopic car-following-based models for lane-free, heterogeneous traffic)
maintainer: MTM: Venkatesan Kanagaraj and Martin Treiber (TU Dresden). IAM: Martin Treiber and Ankit Anil Chaudhari (TU Dresden). NLBIDM: authors not confirmed; paper in a ScienceDirect journal (article id S0968090X26002366, the Transportation Research Part C prefix) calibrated on Chennai data [uncertain].
first_release: MTM: arXiv 1805.05076 submitted 2018-05-14, Physica A 509 (2018) 1-11. IAM: arXiv 2310.16816 submitted 2023-10-25. NLBIDM: about 2026 [uncertain].
last_activity: NLBIDM journal article about 2026 [uncertain]; reference implementation of MTM/IAM in MTGermany/mixedTraffic last committed 2026-04-30.
licence: Papers: arXiv versions publicly readable (licence of each arXiv version not checked [uncertain]). Only open code is MTGermany/mixedTraffic under GPL-3.0. NLBIDM: no code licence found [uncertain].
language: MTM and IAM reference implementation in JavaScript (MTGermany/mixedTraffic); MTM calibration was done with MATLAB's genetic algorithm. NLBIDM implementation language unknown [uncertain].
code_availability: MTM and IAM: source available at https://github.com/MTGermany/mixedTraffic (js/models.js class MTM; IAM scenarios sim_lanes_IAM.js and sim_bicycles_IAM.js) with live demo at https://www.mtreiber.de/mixedTraffic/ (the IAM paper cites it as the online demonstration). The arXiv page for IAM lists no paper-specific code or data. NLBIDM: paper only, no public repository found [uncertain].
maintenance_health: MTM/IAM: research line still active (IAM 2023, Kulkarni, Chaudhari, Treiber et al. leader-follower calibration on Chennai data published in Transportation Research Part C 2024/2025, DOI 10.1016/j.trc.2024.104940); single-author JS code. NLBIDM: new single paper.
scale: Microscopic, time-continuous, two-dimensional (longitudinal x along road axis, lateral y), ballistic update.
car_following: All three wrap an underlying car-following model. MTM: any acceleration CF model split into free part f_self(v)=a_CF(s->inf,v,v) and interaction part a_CF,int=a_CF-a_free; used with the ACC model (IDM extension) in calibration; also tested with IDM, OVM and Gipps. The CF model must return -b_max (9 m/s2 in calibration) for negative gaps. Longitudinal force from the single strongest leader l' = argmax|f_il|: f_il = alpha(dy) * a_CF,int(dx, v_i, v_l) with alpha = min(exp(-s_y/s0y), 1), s_y = |dy| - (W_i+W_l)/2. IAM: same structure with IDM; total longitudinal interaction = min over leaders + max over followers' push term (-lambda * f_ji), so a truck reacts only to the slowest/nearest of several parallel cyclists. NLBIDM: IDM extended with minimum lateral clearance, dynamic pseudo lane, centerline separation ratio, vehicle-specific parameters, systematic leader selection, steady-state and local/string stability analysis (from abstract; equations not retrieved) [uncertain].
lane_model: MTM and IAM: no lanes; optional floor field turns them into an integrated car-following and continuous lane-changing model. IAM floor field: g_lane = -dPhi/dy, Phi = +/-Phi0 cos(2 pi y / W_lane), max induced lateral acceleration 2 pi Phi0 / W_lane; a phase shift of pi gives motorcycles their own between-lane paths. NLBIDM: 'dynamic pseudo lane' around each vehicle instead of painted lanes [uncertain].
lateral_model_type: MTM and IAM: continuous 2D, force-based (social-force-like with CF kinematics). NLBIDM: primarily longitudinal model with lateral-offset-dependent leader selection and interaction (pseudo-lane), not a full lateral dynamics model [uncertain].
junction_model: None of the three models defines junction conflict resolution. MTM and IAM represent red traffic lights and stop signs as very short, very wide standing virtual vehicles covering the stop line, considered separately from the real leader. The tactical lateral component (entering or leaving a road) is a placeholder of order 1 m/s2 not modelled in the MTM paper; IAM uses a desired lateral speed w0 = v0 * e_dest,y toward a destination.
signal_control_modes: Not part of the models; signals enter only as virtual standing obstacles.
vehicle_types: MTM calibration: motorcycle, car, bus, auto-rickshaw (no trucks present in the recorded video). MTM/IAM code: car, truck, bike (bicycle or motorbike), obstacle. IAM paper: cars, motorcycles (Athens), bicycles. Classes differ by length, width and CF parameters; lateral parameters are shared across classes in MTM.
gridlock_policy: Not applicable at model level. MTM includes a fix so vehicles overlapping a leader that is too close to a boundary steer to the passable side; in code an angle-restriction lift (speedLatStuck) avoids getting stuck behind obstacles.
mixed_traffic_support: Yes: the explicit purpose of all three. MTM/IAM let any vehicle pass any other where the lateral gap exceeds the average half-widths; interaction strength depends on lateral overlap. NLBIDM adds vehicle-specific parameters and minimum lateral clearance per pair [uncertain].
non_lane_behaviour: MTM lateral dynamics: g_i = g_self + g_boundary + g_int. g_int = (w0_i - w_i)/tau (OVM-like relaxation), with desired lateral speed w0_i = sum over neighbours j of w0_ij = lambda * alpha_tilde(dy_ij) * a_CF,int_ij * [1 - lambda_dw * (w_j - w_i) * sign(dy_ij)], where alpha_tilde = sign(dy)*(1 + s_y/W) for overlap (s_y<0) and sign(dy)*exp(-s_y/s_tilde_y0) otherwise. This is MOBIL's acceleration-difference incentive turned into a derivative of the longitudinal force with respect to y. Followers are included with weight p (politeness); p>0 gives an automatic MOBIL-like safety criterion because overlapping neighbours return -b_max. Heading is limited to a cone of half-angle theta. Boundaries: longitudinal f_b = -b_b (v/v0) exp(-s_yb/s0b) and lateral g_b = +/- b_tilde_b (v/v0) exp(-s_yb/s_tilde_0b); the v/v0 factor lets slow vehicles squeeze through narrow gaps. IAM simplifies: g_int_ij = (w0_ij - w_i)/tau_y with w0_ij = sigma * f_CF,int * (dy/W if overlapping, else sign(dy) exp(-s_y/s0y)), summed over all agents without shielding, followers weighted by anisotropy lambda; boundary force vector alpha_B(s_y)*(-f_B*v/v0, +/- g_B), alpha_B = min(1, exp(-s/s_B0)). IAM paper criticises MTM for reacting only to front vehicles and for lateral forces that are hard to calibrate.
seepage_filtering_support: Yes, emergent in MTM/IAM: narrow vehicles steer laterally into gaps and pass wider ones; IAM reproduced motorcycles riding between lanes in Athens pNEUMA data via a phase-shifted floor field. Queue-front accumulation at signals is not explicitly validated in either paper [uncertain]. NLBIDM: not stated.
per_class_parameters: MTM, calibrated on Chennai (Table 1, ACC model, b_max = 9 m/s2): Motorcycle L=1.8 m, W=0.6 m, v0 range printed '25-18' m/s, T=0.3 s, s0=0.5 m, a=2.0, b=2.0 m/s2; Car L=4.2, W=1.7, v0 18-12 m/s, T=0.8 s, s0=2.0 m, a=1.0, b=1.0; Bus L=10.3, W=2.1, v0 14-10 m/s, T=1.0 s, s0=2.0, a=1.0, b=1.0; Auto-rickshaw L=2.6, W=0.9, v0 printed '5-6' m/s, T=1.0 s, s0=2.0, a=1.0, b=1.0 (the motorcycle and auto-rickshaw v0 ranges look like typesetting errors, treat with caution [uncertain]). MTM lateral parameters (Table 2, calibrated): theta=0.2 rad, s0y=0.15 m, s_tilde_y0=0.30 m, s0b=0.15 m, s_tilde_0b=0.25 m, lambda=0.4 s, tau=1 s, lambda_dw=0.7 s/m, p=0.2. IAM typical values (Table 1, not Indian-calibrated): tau_y=1 s, s0y=0.3 m, s_B0=0.2 m, lambda=0 to 0.2, sigma=1 s, f_B=0.2 m/s2, g_B=5 m/s2. NLBIDM per-class values: not retrieved [uncertain].
indian_calibration_evidence: MTM: calibrated on medium traffic and validated on congested traffic at a Chennai urban arterial midblock. Calibration (medium): travel time 7.24 s observed vs 6.16 s simulated, SD 3.02 vs 3.90 s, entry flow 2.79 vs 2.42 veh/s, exit flow 1.96 vs 2.21 veh/s, lateral shifts 11 vs 14. Validation (congested, parameters unchanged): travel time 12.82 vs 13.41 s, SD 7.28 vs 5.95 s, entry 1.87 vs 1.79 veh/s, exit 2.31 vs 2.68 veh/s, lateral shifts 14 vs 9. Authors: all within 20% except lateral shifts in validation. IAM: validated on Athens (pNEUMA) arterial and bicycle data, not Indian data. NLBIDM: calibrated on high-resolution Chennai trajectory data (results not retrieved) [uncertain]. Related: Kulkarni, Chaudhari, Srinivasan, Chilukuri, Treiber, Okhrin (arXiv 2405.10665, TR-C) jointly identify leader-follower pairs and calibrate following parameters on Chennai non-lane-based data, reporting better results than heuristic pairings.
calibration_dataset_used: MTM: video of a 250 m homogeneous section of a divided urban road in Chennai, nominal six lanes and 12 m width per roadway, medium and congested snapshots (left-hand traffic), 20 s simulations, 47 m test section. Probably the open Kanagaraj, Asaithambi, Toledo and Lee (TRR 2491, 2015) dataset from the Maraimalai Adigalar Bridge, Saidapet, Chennai, which is distributed by Technion as two 15-minute CSV files (2:45-3:00 pm and 3:00-3:15 pm) with about 3,005 vehicle trajectories at 0.5 s resolution [uncertain that MTM used exactly this file]. IAM: open pNEUMA drone data (Athens, Leof. Alexandras, 24 Oct 2018). NLBIDM: Chennai high-resolution trajectories [uncertain which].
calibration_method: MTM: MATLAB standard genetic algorithm minimising S = sqrt(sum over 5 measures of ((X_sim - X_obs)/X_obs)^2) over mean travel time, travel-time SD, entry flow, exit flow and count of lateral shifts (lateral move > 1 m in one direction plus leader change). Initial conditions taken from observed positions; no inflow during the 20 s run. IAM: qualitative comparison of simulated and observed trajectories and lateral distributions. Kulkarni et al.: joint leader-follower identification and parameter estimation with Wiedemann-99 influence zones. NLBIDM: not retrieved [uncertain].
max_density_tested: MTM validation: about 790 veh/km on one 12 m roadway (450 motorcycles, 225 cars, 35 buses, 80 auto-rickshaws per km, 1D partial densities).
validation_against_field_case: MTM: Chennai six-lane urban arterial midblock (likely Saidapet) [uncertain]. IAM: Athens Leof. Alexandras arterial and bicycle-path capacity experiments. No junction-level Indian field case (no Hebbal or Silk Board validation).
reuse_mode: Port the model. Implement a simplified IAM/MTM (IDM or ACC longitudinal core, exponential lateral attenuation, summed lateral OVM relaxation, boundary forces, heading cap) inside our own link-based engine, and seed per-class longitudinal parameters from MTM Table 1. NLBIDM is inspiration only until its equations and parameters are available.
effort_within_72_hours: MTM/IAM core equations: about 200 to 400 lines; 6 to 10 hours to implement and unit-test (single-file reversion to IDM, no-collision at overlap, boundary containment), plus 4 to 8 hours of tuning. Use IAM's simpler lateral formula and MTM's Chennai longitudinal parameters, set follower pushing to 0 (or lambda about 0.1), fix lambda_dw to 0 initially. Cut: floor fields, calibration pipeline, NLBIDM, per-pair parameters, lateral tactical routing through junctions (use straight-line junction paths with gap acceptance instead). A spatial grid for neighbour search is needed for more than a few hundred vehicles.
licence_constraint: Equations from published papers can be reimplemented freely. Copying the JavaScript reference implementation (MTGermany/mixedTraffic) imposes GPL-3.0 on distributed client code.
known_limitations: MTM: tactical lateral component (entering/leaving roads, keep-left rules) not modelled; no junction behaviour; lateral parameters shared across vehicle classes; calibrated on only two 20 s snapshots of one midblock section using macroscopic measures, so microscopic accuracy is unproven; lateral shifts under-predicted in congestion, possibly due to aggressive or cooperative behaviour not in the model; requires the CF model to return -b_max at negative gaps; the IAM authors note the MTM reacts only to front vehicles and has lateral forces hard to calibrate. IAM: validated on lane-based Athens data and bicycles, not truly lane-free mixed vehicular traffic (left as future work); pushing lambda=1 destroys the fundamental diagram. Code notes: vehicles can leave the road under strong pushes. NLBIDM: longitudinal focus; lateral dynamics and junctions likely out of scope [uncertain]. Literature review (Asaithambi, Kanagaraj, Toledo 2016) notes most non-lane-based models are not estimated rigorously against trajectory data.
documented_failures: MTM: number of lateral shifts in the congested validation off by about 36% (14 observed vs 9 simulated). Reference code: lateral crashes for tau > about 1 s without the relative-lateral-speed term (sensdvy), vehicles leaving the road at high speed or abrupt obstacle ends, vehicles trapped behind slow leaders near boundaries (needed a special-case override). Leader identification in non-lane traffic is itself error-prone: hEART 2025 work on the Saidapet data shows heuristic leader-follower pairing gives R-squared 0.268 vs 0.349 with an improved method.
validation_approach: MTM: plausibility tests on standard situations (overtaking, narrowing, zipper merge) plus GA calibration on medium Chennai traffic and out-of-sample validation on congested traffic with unchanged parameters. IAM: simulations in lane-based and lane-free geometries compared qualitatively with pNEUMA trajectories and bicycle self-organisation (three-lane to two-lane transition 30 m upstream of a bottleneck). NLBIDM: calibration on Chennai trajectories plus analytical steady-state and stability analysis [uncertain].
takeaway_for_our_build: Adopt the IAM form as our link-level physics: acceleration vector = CF free term + strongest-leader CF interaction times exp(-lateral gap/s0y) + boundary force; lateral = summed OVM relaxation toward a desired lateral speed from neighbours, capped, with heading limit about 0.2 rad. Use MTM's published Chennai values (motorcycle T=0.3 s, s0=0.5 m; car T=0.8 s; bus and auto-rickshaw T=1.0 s; s0y=0.15 m; s_tilde_y0=0.30 m; lambda=0.4 s; tau=1 s; p=0.2) as defaults, labelled 'calibrated on one Chennai midblock, not junctions'. Add hard boundary clamping and a regression test that single-file traffic reproduces plain IDM. Do not promise junction realism: no published lane-free model covers Indian junction conflicts, so present junction results as indicative.
